analysis.investment_thesis: Carborundum Universal is a quality abrasives and industrial ceramics business, but at INR 17,909 Cr market cap and P/E of 74x, it is nowhere near the SMILE sweet spot. Net profit collapsed from INR 476 Cr in 2024 to INR 299 Cr in 2025 on negative other income, and revenue CAGR of 10.8% over 9 years is uninspiring.
key_strengths: Near-zero leverage with D/E of 0.08 and strong balance sheet (equity INR 3,745 Cr)
Diversified business across abrasives, technical ceramics, electrominerals — exposure to defence and semiconductor tailwinds
Consistent OCF generation across all 5 years with ROCE of 16%
key_risks: Promoter holding of only 38.9% — well below my 50% minimum; not enough skin in the game
P/E of 74x for a business growing revenue at 10.8% CAGR is unjustifiable — massive valuation risk
Net profit fell 37% YoY (476→299 Cr) in FY25 due to other income turning negative; FCF crashed to just INR 28 Cr
red_flags: Market cap INR 17,909 Cr — 18x outside my sweet spot
P/E 74x on decelerating, low-single-digit ROE (10.8%) business
Promoter holding 38.9% — declining skin in the game
Revenue CAGR of just 10.8% in 9 years — not a multibagger growth profile
analysis.detailed_analysis:
CARBORUNIV is an established, respected industrial company founded in 1954, but it scores poorly on every SMILE criterion. At INR 17,909 Cr market cap, it is a large-cap — not the undiscovered small-cap where I find asymmetric opportunities. The P/E of 74x (forward 39x) implies the market is pricing in a transformation that 9-year revenue CAGR of 10.8% and operating margin of 7.43% simply do not support.

FY25 was a warning sign — net profit fell sharply to INR 299 Cr from INR 476 Cr as other income swung to -INR 23 Cr, and FCF nearly evaporated (INR 28 Cr vs INR 367 Cr in FY24). Promoter holding at 38.9% is below my non-negotiable 50% floor. This is a solid business to hold, not a multibagger to buy at these prices.
